description:
runtime/src/heap/gc/forward.rs: a root holding a boxed scalar (an AnyValueRef whose tag is_scalar, not a literal) is copied by copy_scalar_box_to_space, which calls copy_object_to_space and writes no forwarding marker; cheney_forward_object, the heap-object path beside it, checks forwarded_target first and calls write_forwarding_marker after copying. So two roots naming one scalar box get two 16-byte copies instead of sharing one, and copied_bytes counts both.

Done when: scalar boxes are forwarded like every other object (check forwarded_target, write the marker), ideally by routing them through the same forwarding function rather than a second copier; a heap test with two roots on one scalar box asserts both roots read the same to-space address and copied_bytes counts 16 once. Full gate green (cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1; cargo test --workspace --doc); any pin that moves only goes down and the commit names each with its mechanism; commit in Why / What changed / Verification form; no co-author trailer, no attribution line.
title: Copying a root's scalar box leaves a forwarding marker
